title: Imaging and Quantification of the Area of Fast-Moving Microbubbles Using a High-Speed Camera and Image Analysis
protocol: Select the ultrasonic scaler for imaging.
Place the ultrasonic scaler on a micro positioning stage with XYZ translation and rotation capabilities.
Attach the ultrasonic scaler handle to the micro positioning stage.
Create an optically transparent water container using glass microscope slides.
Fill the water container with filtered water (reverse osmosis or distilled).
Position the water container on an XY stage with a rotation platform.
Select a high-speed camera with desired frame rate and resolution.
Choose a high intensity light source with fibre light guide.
Attach a micropositioning sliding plate to the high-speed camera body.
Connect the high-speed camera to a tripod stand.
Select a zoom lens with resolution of 8.4 µm/pixel and attach it to the camera.
Fill the imaging tank with water.
Position the tip of the ultrasonic scaler in the water tank in the desired orientation.
Use low magnification to focus on the tip of the ultrasonic scaler.
Reposition the light source if necessary.
Position the instrument and the light source in front of the camera and focus.
Adjust to the desired frame rate and brightness.
Set an optimal frame rate and shutter speed for the high-speed camera.
Choose a reference point, such as the tip of the ultrasonic scaler, for reproducibility.
Record the position of the tip (rotation in x-y stage, rotation angle of instrument).
Note down the coordinates of the reference point.
Image the instrument without cavitation for background subtraction.
Save videos in TIFF format to maintain image quality.
Image the instrument operating with cavitation, ensuring sufficient frames are recorded.
Crop images to remove darker areas due to uneven illumination.
Ensure all images are cropped to the same size and location.
Convert images to binary using minimum auto thresholding.
Run the fill holes command to eliminate black pixels falsely segmented inside bubbles.
Calculate the histogram of the image stack to show the number of pixels for scaler and cavitation in each frame.
Repeat steps for the video of the instrument operating without bubbles.
Calculate the mean area of the ultrasonic scaler tip from histogram results.
Subtract the mean area of the instrument from areas calculated from videos with bubbles.
Visualize by subtracting binary image of the scaler from binary image of the scaler with bubbles using ImageJ's image calculator.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the bubble area.
Convert values from number of pixels to area (in this case µm²) by multiplying by pixel size squared.
Determine the size of each pixel by imaging a graticule with high-speed camera at same magnification as used for bubbles, then set scale in ImageJ.
Plot the data.
Conduct statistical analysis to show any significant difference in bubble area if comparing different conditions.
